applications.name: Warehouse and Distribution
applications.description:
Lift tables in a warehouse spend their life on pallets. They raise a pallet so the top layer stays at a comfortable working height while it is built or broken down, they bring a load up to a conveyor or a packing bench, and they replace the bending that hand palletizing otherwise guarantees.

The decision that matters most here is how the pallet gets onto the table. A forklift can place a load on any lift table; a hand pallet truck cannot reach one unless the deck comes almost to the floor, which is why low profile, floor level and U-shaped platforms dominate this list. Self-leveling pallet positioners deserve a look too: they sink under each layer added and rise as layers are removed, holding the top of the stack steady without any controls at all.
applications.supporting:
Two things decide whether a lift table earns its place in a warehouse, and neither is capacity. The first is how the pallet arrives: a table a hand truck cannot reach will be loaded by hand instead, which is the injury it was bought to prevent. The second is the cycle rate — a table on a packing line runs hundreds of times a day and needs a power unit specified for it.

If loads are built or broken down by hand, look at pallet positioners before anything else. A self-leveling table holds the top of the stack at a constant height with no controls at all, and a turntable on top of one removes the reach across the pallet that causes most of the remaining strain.

applications.name: Assembly and Production
applications.description:
On a production line a lift table is a work positioner. It brings the part to the operator at the height and angle that suits the job, feeds a machine at a fixed deck height, and holds the work steady while something is done to it.

Two specifications decide whether one of these succeeds. The first is duty cycle: a table raised twice a shift and a table cycling every two minutes need different power units, and it is the specification most often left out of an enquiry. The second is the control — a foot switch keeps both hands on the work, a hand pendant suits an operator standing beside the table, and constant-pressure controls matter anywhere someone could be caught by the platform.
applications.supporting:
An assembly station is the one place a lift table is judged on its controls as much as its capacity. A foot switch keeps both hands on the work. A hand pendant suits an operator standing to one side. Constant-pressure controls, where the platform stops the moment the button is released, matter anywhere a person could be caught by it.

Duty cycle is the specification most often left out of an enquiry here and the one that decides whether the table is still working in five years. Give the cycles per hour and the hours per day, and say whether the table is part of a machine cycle rather than somewhere to put things — a press stroke or a robot placing a part is not the static load the rating describes.

applications.name: Food and Beverage
applications.description:
Food, dairy, bakery and beverage plants wash their equipment down, often daily and often with chemicals that make short work of painted carbon steel. A lift table specified for these areas is built differently from the start: stainless construction, continuous welds ground smooth, open frames and sloped surfaces that shed water rather than hold it.

Two details are ordered with the table or not at all. The grade has to suit the chemistry — 304 handles most food work, 316 resists chlorides and brine — and the power unit has to match the washdown, which means a sealed enclosure rating and, in most plants, food-grade hydraulic fluid. A stainless deck on a general-purpose power unit fails at the enclosure.
applications.supporting:
The largest price difference in this category is one question: how much of the table has to be stainless. A stainless deck and covers on a painted carbon steel frame, and a table where the scissor legs, pins and hardware are stainless too, are both sold as stainless lift tables. Pin that down before comparing quotes.

Then match the details to the washdown. 304 handles most food work and 316 resists chlorides and brine, so ask which grade is quoted. Specify a sealed enclosure rating on the power unit and, in most plants, food-grade hydraulic fluid — both are ordered with the table rather than fitted afterward.

applications.name: Pharmaceutical and Cleanroom
applications.description:
Cleanroom and pharmaceutical work rules out most of what a standard lift table is made of. Hydraulic oil is a contamination risk, painted surfaces shed, and anywhere particles can collect is somewhere that has to be cleaned and validated.

The tables that suit these rooms solve it in one of two ways. Oil-free designs — pneumatic bellows, electric linear actuators, mechanical screw drives — remove the fluid entirely. Full stainless construction in 304 or 316, with no closed tubes or pockets, makes what remains cleanable. Both routes are represented below, and both are specified at order rather than retrofitted.
applications.supporting:
Cleanroom work splits lift tables into two routes. Oil-free designs — pneumatic bellows, electric linear actuators, mechanical screw drives — remove hydraulic fluid from the room entirely, which is the cleanest answer where contamination is the governing risk. Full stainless construction in 304 or 316, with continuous welds and no closed tubes or pockets, makes what remains cleanable and validatable.

Say which classification the room is and what the cleaning regime is when you enquire. Both change the specification, and neither can be added to a table that has already been built.
